item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
One minor thing that could be done would be to break up the paragraphs more when you want to get across a sense of a faster pace. Good for action. It's a cheap little technique, but it might help a little.

That's an interesting point, and instead I see that have done nearly the opposite of that, where the more uneventful parts are short paragraphs and the engagements are long and detailed. Partially this is because the purpose of these things is to inform future training and procedures, and so the detail focus on where it isn't a controlled situation and lessons can be learned is needed. Also though I think I was perhaps subconsciously relating the way that time feels when things become "kinetic", seconds stretch out and certain details become hyper-emphasized in your memory. I am not sure if splitting up the kinetic paragraphs more wouldn't have an effect that is opposite to putting the reader into the action, actually.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As in their first story, this reminded me heavily of games (In this case, SCP-themed Darkest Dungeon).

This is clearly a different kind of Foundation (and world) than the one many of the stories are set in, with an almost World of Darkness-y secret but open warfare feeling instead of a mostly normal world with terrifying but often subtle, local or missable phenomena that need to be contained. Under these conditions, the other documents make a lot more sense, especially Avatara's "we found four SCPs. Let's use them in the field!" - I think my opinion of the whole set of articles was lifted by this one.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There have been few things on this site that have switched between boring and entertaining as much as this AAR.

Well, I guess I aim to be unique.

I was concerned about it being too dry, but I enjoy reading these things in real life (at least those involving interesting actions) and have written reports that contributed to real ones too. I cut a lot of corners here for entertainment purposes, and I don't think that I would have been personally comfortable with much less authenticity here.

+ How the sausage was made
- And knowing is half the battle! GI Joe!

Echoing what others have said, the technobabble about the Paratech in the first section is pretty hit and miss. Some objects are interesting to read about, others made my eyes glaze over. None of this was enough to convince me to stop reading, as the interesting tech was particularly interesting.

That went through a few variations when writing this, but ultimately, if Tau-5 is tasked with testing this stuff, some detail probably makes sense here. I honestly don't know which items make your eyes glaze over, all of these items were fun to invent and I tried to keep to a short list that fit the threat profile — that would still seem like enough of a force multiplier to make the four man "squad" that my teammates insisted on viable (essentially this organization is treating them more like IFVs than individual infantrymen, and they needed the survibility to match).

On a different note, there is a fair amount of blacking out in this, and I am a little puzzled as to why.

Entirely meta reasons, I am afraid.

For the location, I could guess that the higher ranks don't want the reader to poke around the mission location, which is fine.

The real reason is that with the short deadline, I really didn't have time to poke around extensively in satellite photos and write the operation around a real building.

It should be somewhere around 29RPQ1926394068, though.

As for that first date, I am lost as to why that needed to be blacked out.

That is entirely an oversight, I had meant to fill that in as we got the timeline worked out, but forgot. I'll find out if fixing this is within the contest rules.

Getting into the description of the event, I felt like it played out very much like a fast paced action movie at some parts, and slowed to a crawl at others, which made the flow kind of choppy.

Well, that is combat: periods of intense boredom punctuated by terror. Earlier versions had even more "boring" stuff, but I was eventually persuaded to cut them. Short of ignoring vital operational details (making Hughes look incompetent) or having them teleport into position, or just writing this like the world according to Michael Bay, I don't think that I could really cut much more.

While a good chunk of this is drier than the Sahara

Perhaps appropriate given the location…

ETA: Edits were approved and made! Dates filled along with the MGRS map reference.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Without some effective countermeasures the Foundation would be unable to cope with working magic altogether (and this series takes place in a world where PL was developing commercial applications of weird science; which people actually paid for and used). If a wholly conventional team had attempted this raid, they would have just died. Eventually it would be fairly impossible for the Foundation to find people willing to go on utterly symbolic suicide missions in order to prove some ideological purity.
